findings.quote: a pure compound has the same mass ratio of its elements, whatever its source.
findings.problem: This absolute ignores differences in isotopic composition. For example, carbon dioxide containing carbon-13 has a different carbon-to-oxygen mass ratio from carbon dioxide containing carbon-12, even though both have one carbon atom per two oxygen atoms. Constant atomic ratios imply constant mass ratios only when the isotope composition is held fixed.
findings.source: [IUPAC CIAAW: Carbon](https://www.ciaaw.org/carbon.htm), which gives different carbon isotope masses and documents source-dependent isotopic composition.
